mainEntity.name: Can I change the look, the voice, or the language?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Pick from 53 actors and choose a voice or language that fits your audience. You can reuse the same presenter across ads.

mainEntity.name: Are AI actors good for product explainers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. An AI actor can explain product features clearly and consistently. Update the message in minutes without booking another shoot.

mainEntity.name: How can brands use AI actors for social media?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep one AI actor across a series of social posts and change the opening each time. You can make more versions without filming again.

mainEntity.name: How do AI actors make videos?

acceptedAnswer.text: Type your message, choose an actor and voice, and generate a video. The actor speaks the words with matching lip movement, ready for you to review.

mainEntity.name: Can I update training videos with an AI actor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Change the message and make a new training video. You can keep lessons current without bringing a presenter back to a studio.

mainEntity.name: What is an AI actor?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a realistic digital presenter for your video. Choose its look and voice to explain your product without filming a person.

mainEntity.name: Where can I use AI actors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use an AI actor in product ads, website videos, social posts, and short explainers. You can keep the same presenter across channels.

mainEntity.name: Can I use AI actors commercially?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. AI actor videos have no watermark and can be used commercially. Starter costs $24.50 monthly for 200 credits, Pro $35 for 300, and Premium $63 for 600.

mainEntity.name: What should I know before using an AI actor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell viewers when a presenter is AI if the platform requires it. Do not impersonate a real customer or use someone’s face or voice without permission.

mainEntity.name: How do I make a before and after video from one photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload a clear starting photo and describe the result you want to show. Generate the video, then check that the change matches your product.

mainEntity.name: What does a before and after product video show?

acceptedAnswer.text: A before-and-after video shows the starting point and the visible result of using your product. Put both views together so shoppers see the change quickly.

mainEntity.name: How many credits does a before-and-after video use?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 6-second video uses 24 credits; 10, 15, and 30 seconds use 40, 60, and 120. Failed videos return their credits.

mainEntity.name: Can TikTok or Meta reject a before-and-after ad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the ad breaks their rules or makes a misleading claim. Check each platform’s current policy before running it.

mainEntity.name: Which products fit a before and after video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Products with a visible change work best, such as cleaning supplies, skincare, and home improvements. Show a real result that matches what buyers can expect.

mainEntity.name: Can I make before-and-after videos for many products?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Use each product’s photo to make its own before-and-after video. You can create more ads without scheduling separate shoots.

mainEntity.name: Can the file run as an ad I paid for?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Commercial use is part of a paid plan, and the download has no watermark. You still need rights to the photo you uploaded.

mainEntity.name: Which video shapes can I download?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can download 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4. Use the tall file for TikTok, the square for a feed, or the wide file for a landscape placement.

mainEntity.name: Can an AI avatar narrate the change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Choose an AI actor to explain the change while the video shows your product. You do not need to hire a presenter.

mainEntity.name: Will a white background make my product look flat?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, if your source photo has clear lighting and contrast. A soft natural shadow adds depth while keeping attention on the item.

mainEntity.name: How do I put a product photo onto pure white?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload your photo and choose pure white, RGB 255, 255, 255. Review the product edges, then download the image for your listing.

mainEntity.name: How many credits does one photo use?

acceptedAnswer.text: One white-background image costs 24 credits. You see the cost before starting, and a failed job returns those credits.

mainEntity.name: Does a marketplace main image have to sit on white?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many marketplaces require a pure white main image. Check your category’s current rules, because a background that only looks white may fail an automated check.

mainEntity.name: How do I add a white background to a product photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload your product photo, and AI removes the room behind it. Download the item on a clean white background without manually cutting around the edges.

mainEntity.name: What should the starting photo show?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a clear photo that shows the whole product and its edges. Good lighting helps you check the result quickly.

mainEntity.name: Can I post the file on Amazon, Shopify, or Etsy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Download the image without a watermark for Amazon, Shopify, Etsy, or paid ads. Check each marketplace’s image rules before posting.

mainEntity.name: Which tool can make a pure white product photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose a tool that removes the original background cleanly and gives you pure white. This one makes a listing-ready image from a product photo.

mainEntity.name: How much does a white-background photo cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: One image costs 24 credits. Starter costs $24.50 monthly for 200 credits, Pro costs $35 for 300, and Premium costs $63 for 600.

mainEntity.name: Can I apply white backgrounds to a whole catalog?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Apply the same white background to many product photos in a batch or through the API. Review each item before publishing its listing.

acceptedAnswer.text: Follow the platform’s current labeling rules when you post an AI image. Requirements vary by platform and location.

mainEntity.name: How much does a social ad image cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each image costs 24 credits. Starter costs $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro costs $35 for 300, and Premium costs $63 for 600.

mainEntity.name: Can I put a headline on the image?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Add a short headline that shoppers can read on a phone. You can also put the headline in the ad text instead.

mainEntity.name: How can I make social posts that stand out?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with a clear product photo and a ready-made scene, then add a short message. Try different backgrounds or colors to see what catches attention.

mainEntity.name: How often should a small shop post?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose a schedule you can keep, then reply to comments. One product photo can become several posts with different scenes.

mainEntity.name: Can one product photo make several social posts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Make several scenes from one product photo and compare them in your posts or ads. You do not need a new shoot.

mainEntity.name: What kinds of social posts work best?

acceptedAnswer.text: Posts with a strong product photo and a clear opening often get attention. Try posts that show, teach, or entertain, then compare the results.

mainEntity.name: Where can I use a square social ad image?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use it in square feed posts and ads on platforms that accept that size. Check your text in each placement before posting.

mainEntity.name: Can I use this for the store and the lookbook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Use matching model photos across product pages and lookbooks. Change the background and lighting to keep the collection consistent.

mainEntity.name: What image sizes can I download?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose tall, square, or wide photos for your store and ads. Available sizes include 9:16, 1:1, 4:3, 16:9, and 3:4.

mainEntity.name: How close is a virtual model to a studio photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Virtual model photos can look like studio images with natural poses and light. Check fabric, fit, and small details against the real item before publishing.

mainEntity.name: How does a virtual model photo get made for clothing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload a clear garment photo and choose a virtual model. The tool places your clothing on a lifelike person with natural lighting, without a studio shoot.

mainEntity.name: What if a small print looks different?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check each finished photo against the garment before posting. If a print or seam looks wrong, change the image and make another version.

mainEntity.name: Can I put my own products on a virtual model?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Upload the clothing or accessory you sell and choose a virtual model to wear it. You can make catalog photos in minutes.

mainEntity.name: Can I publish these photos on my store and in ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Use watermark-free model photos on product pages and in paid ads. Keep a clear product photo alongside them when shoppers need to inspect details.

mainEntity.name: Can I make virtual model photos through an API?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can send garment photos from your store software through the API. This helps create model photos for a large catalog.

mainEntity.name: How can virtual models help my fashion shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: They put your clothing on lifelike models without a shoot. Make consistent photos for product pages, lookbooks, and ads in minutes.

mainEntity.name: Can I create model photos for an entire collection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Create on-model photos for each item or color in your collection. One photo costs 24 credits, so you can plan the cost before starting.

step.name: Upload Your Side Photos
step.text: Upload a clear photo of each product side you need. Keep the whole item in frame and the lighting even.

step.name: Describe Your Scene
step.text: Name the view and request the same plain backdrop. Use the photo of that side when buttons or ports must stay accurate.

mainEntity.name: Can I make packshots without editing experience?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Upload a clear product photo and choose the view. You do not need editing experience to make a clean listing image.

mainEntity.name: How do I make a matching set of product views?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload clear photos of the sides you want to show. Use the same background and lighting to make a consistent product gallery.

mainEntity.name: Where can I use the finished photos?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use them in product galleries, marketplaces, social posts, or paid ads. Download the photos without a watermark.

mainEntity.name: What if I have no photo of the back or top?

acceptedAnswer.text: Photograph and upload any side that shows an important detail. This keeps the finished image accurate for your buyers.

mainEntity.name: How many credits does a packshot use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each product photo costs 24 credits. The cost appears before you start, and failed jobs return their credits.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the product photos in paid ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Use the watermark-free images in paid ads and product pages. Check each view against the real item before posting.

mainEntity.name: Can I use photos I already took?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Upload your own photos of each side for accurate details. Clear source images help the finished views look realistic.

mainEntity.name: Who needs multi-angle product photos?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any shop selling products with details on several sides can use them. Show buttons, openings, or the base so buyers know what to expect.

mainEntity.name: What are multi-angle product photos?

acceptedAnswer.text: They show your product from the front, side, back, or top. Matching views help shoppers understand its shape before buying.

mainEntity.name: Why keep the same background for every side?

acceptedAnswer.text: A matching background makes the views easier to compare. Shoppers can focus on the product’s shape and details.

mainEntity.name: Which products work for multi-angle packshots?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bags, mugs, electronics, and other physical goods work well. Choose views that help shoppers inspect the product before buying.

mainEntity.name: Why use these photos instead of another shoot?

acceptedAnswer.text: They give you matching product views without setting up another studio shoot. You can update a listing in minutes.

@graph.name: AI Professional Headshots for Teams | AIVideosUGC
@graph.description: Create matching professional headshots from approved team photos. Choose one backdrop and crop, then download portraits for your About page and profiles.

@graph.name: How to Make Team Headshots in 3 Simple Steps

step.name: Upload Each Team Photo
step.text: Add a clear, approved face-and-shoulders photo for each teammate.

step.name: Pick One Background
step.text: Choose one professional backdrop, crop, and lighting direction for the team.

step.name: Download and Post
step.text: Review each face, then download portraits for your team page and profiles.

mainEntity.name: Can clients use the portraits I create?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the person in the portrait agrees to that use. Review the final image before putting it on a client site or in a presentation.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a photographer for professional headshots?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Upload a face photo and choose a professional style. You can make team headshots without booking a photographer or learning editing software.

mainEntity.name: How do I make a professional headshot with AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload a clear, approved photo of each person and choose a professional background. Review the finished headshot before downloading it.

mainEntity.name: Can I use photos my team already approved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Use only photos and likenesses your teammates have approved for this purpose. Review each result with them before publishing.

mainEntity.name: What kind of source photo works best?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose a sharp, front-facing photo with even light and a clear view of the face. This helps the finished portrait look like the person.

mainEntity.name: Can I try different backgrounds and crops?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Try different professional backgrounds and crops, then choose one style for the team. You can make new versions without another photo session.

mainEntity.name: How do I add a new teammate later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload an approved photo of the new teammate and reuse your team’s background and crop. Check that the new portrait fits beside the others.

mainEntity.name: Can I make matching headshots for my team?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Use the same background, lighting, and crop for each person. Your team portraits can look consistent without scheduling one studio day.

mainEntity.name: Will an AI headshot still look like me?

acceptedAnswer.text: It should. Start with a clear photo and compare the result with the person before publishing. Make another version if the face looks wrong.

mainEntity.name: Where can I use professional headshots?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use approved headshots on your team page, LinkedIn, speaker bios, and proposals. Get each person’s permission for where their portrait appears.

mainEntity.name: How much does an AI headshot cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: One headshot costs 24 credits. Starter costs $24.50 monthly for 200 credits, Pro costs $35 for 300, and Premium costs $63 for 600.

@graph.name: Instagram Sales Post Maker | AIVideosUGC
@graph.description: Make an Instagram sales post that puts your discount and your event in the spotlight. Start from a ready square, add your offer, and post it.

@graph.name: How to Make an Instagram Sale Post in 3 Simple Steps

step.name: Upload Your Product Photo
step.text: Upload one clear photo of the product on sale. The template gives you a square made for the feed.

step.name: Pick a Sale Scene
step.text: Leave an open area for the code and the dates. The offer should be what shoppers read first.

step.name: Download and Post
step.text: Download the square and publish it on Instagram once the offer is easy to read.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a paid plan for sale images?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Starter costs $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro costs $35 for 300, and Premium costs $63 for 600. Each image uses 24 credits.

mainEntity.name: What does an Instagram sale template give me?

acceptedAnswer.text: It gives you a ready-made square post with room for your product and offer. Add your photo and message without designing from scratch.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the sale image in an Instagram Story?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Place the square image on a 9:16 background so it fits a Story. Check that the offer stays easy to read.

mainEntity.name: How many credits does a sale image cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each sale image costs 24 credits. Failed jobs return credits, and the download has no watermark for ads or posts.

mainEntity.name: Can I change the offer in a holiday sale image?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Keep the product scene and update the headline, code, and date for the next promotion. Check the new offer before posting.

mainEntity.name: Can my sale post show a discount and end date?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Add the discount, code, and end date in large text that shoppers can read. Check every detail before the sale starts.

mainEntity.name: What size is an Instagram sale image?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a square image for Instagram and Facebook feeds. You can place it on a wider or taller background for other uses.

mainEntity.name: What should I do when the sale ends?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replace or pause the post so shoppers do not see an expired offer. Reuse the product scene for a later promotion.

mainEntity.name: Where should I put the discount code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Put the code where it is easy to read on a phone. Check the code and dates before you publish the post.

mainEntity.name: Can I reuse a sale image for another promotion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Keep the product scene and change the offer for your next sale. You do not need a new product photo.

mainEntity.name: How do I make a sale post from one product photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload your photo, choose a sale scene, and add your confirmed offer. Download the square image and check it on a phone before posting.

mainEntity.name: Can I cancel before my next bill?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Cancel in your account before the next billing date. Check your account for when your access ends.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the same product photo for another market?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Use the photo again and add text in the language your shoppers speak. You can make different scenes for each market.

mainEntity.name: Can I change an image before downloading it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Change the scene or crop, then make another version if needed. Each newly generated image uses credits.

mainEntity.name: Can I start from a product link?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Paste a public product link to start a creator-style image. Check that the result matches the product you sell.

mainEntity.name: Which files can I upload to start?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload clear product photos or clips you have permission to use. You can also paste a public product link.

mainEntity.name: What can I change in a creator-style photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Change the setting, crop, and product placement to fit your ad. You can make another version without a new photo shoot.

mainEntity.name: What happens if an image fails?

acceptedAnswer.text: The credits for a failed image return to your balance. Check your account if the balance does not update.

mainEntity.name: Will changing plans create another credit balance?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your account shows the balance for your current plan. Check it after changing plans so you know how many credits are available.

mainEntity.name: Does my plan include monthly credits?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Starter includes 200 credits, Pro includes 300, and Premium includes 600 each month. Use them for images and videos.

mainEntity.name: Can I use creator-style images in paid ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Use downloaded images in your store, social posts, and paid ads without a watermark. Check product details before publishing.

mainEntity.name: How many credits does a creator-style image use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each image uses 24 credits. You see the cost before starting, and failed jobs return credits.

mainEntity.name: Can I edit the image after it is made?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Change the scene or crop and make another version. You can also turn the product photo into a video later.

mainEntity.name: Can I switch my subscription?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Change between Starter, Pro, and Premium in your account. Check the new price and credit amount before confirming.

mainEntity.name: What comes with a monthly plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Starter includes 200 credits for $24.50, Pro includes 300 for $35, and Premium includes 600 for $63 each month. Use credits for product images and ads.

mainEntity.name: Do unused credits carry into the next month?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rollover depends on your current plan terms, which you can check in your account before renewal. Credits from failed jobs return to your balance.

@graph.description: Turn a flat-lay or hanger photo into an on-model clothing image. Show fit, color, and fabric in virtual try-on photos for product listings and ads.

step.text: Upload a clear flat-lay or hanger photo that shows the full garment, including the collar and hem.

mainEntity.name: How can virtual try-on help shoppers?

acceptedAnswer.text: It lets shoppers preview how clothing looks on a person before buying. Upload a garment photo to make an on-model image in minutes.

mainEntity.name: How long does a virtual try-on image take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A virtual try-on image takes a few minutes. Review the garment details, then download it for your product page or ad.

mainEntity.name: How do I create a virtual try-on image?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload a garment photo, choose a model and setting, and make the image. Check its color, print, and fit before adding it to your store.

mainEntity.name: Can my store use virtual try-on photos?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Use on-model images on product pages and in ads. They help shoppers picture the garment, while your size chart still guides fit.

mainEntity.name: Can I make several try-on images for one garment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Make more poses, models, or backgrounds from the same garment photo. Check each version against the real item before posting.

mainEntity.name: What photo do I need for virtual try-on?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload a clear photo of the whole garment. Flat lays and hanger shots work when the fabric, color, and details are easy to see.

mainEntity.name: Do I need technical skills to use virtual try-on?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Upload the garment and choose a model in a few steps. You do not need design or editing skills.

mainEntity.name: What does a virtual try-on photo cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: One virtual try-on image costs 24 credits. You see the cost before starting, and a failed job returns the credits.

mainEntity.name: Can I make a video from one product photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Upload your photo, choose an AI actor and voice, and make a product video without filming. You can change the message later.

mainEntity.name: How long does an AI video take to make?

acceptedAnswer.text: An AI video takes a few minutes to make. You can download it when generation finishes, and failed jobs return credits.

mainEntity.name: How does the AI video generator work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Give it a product photo, link, or idea, then choose the style and voice. It makes a video with visuals and spoken words in a few minutes.

mainEntity.name: Can I make videos for my online store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Make product demos, creator-style ads, or social videos from your photos and links. Use them on product pages or in campaigns.

mainEntity.name: What voices can I use in an AI video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose a bright, calm, or deep voice that fits your product and customers. Preview several voices before posting.

mainEntity.name: Which AI video generator is best for a small shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose one that makes ads from your product photos, shows the credit cost, and lets you change the actor or words. AIVideosUGC does all three.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to install software to make videos?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Make and download your video in the browser. You can add music and captions in the same place.

mainEntity.name: Can a product page link become a video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Paste a public product link to bring in its photos and details. Check the finished video against the product you sell.

mainEntity.name: How do I make an AI product video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload a product photo, paste a product link, or describe your idea. Choose an actor and voice, then make a video in a few minutes.

mainEntity.name: Can I use AI videos in paid ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Downloaded videos can run in paid campaigns without a watermark. Check that every product claim is accurate before posting.

mainEntity.name: Can I run an AI video on Facebook or Instagram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Download the video for Facebook or Instagram ads. Choose a square or vertical size that fits the placement.

mainEntity.name: How much does an AI product video cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Videos cost 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. Starter costs $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro $35 for 300, and Premium $63 for 600.

mainEntity.name: Can I make several versions of one product video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Keep the same product and try different openings, actors, or voices. Compare the versions in your ad account to see what works.

mainEntity.name: Why make product videos with AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can make videos in minutes without a shoot, crew, or creator fees. Try different openings and captions for your ads.

mainEntity.name: Can AI make a news-style product video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Choose a news-style scene, voice, and message. Set the video length and size, then review it before posting.

mainEntity.name: What should I tell the AI video generator?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell it what you sell, who the video is for, and the main benefit to show. Clear product details help make a better first version.

mainEntity.name: Can I choose the actor, voice, size, and length?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Choose an AI actor, voice, video size, and length before you start. The credit cost appears before generation.

settings.body:
1. Scope of this policy

This Privacy Policy explains how AIVideosUGC handles customer accounts, uploaded source photos, generated images and videos, prompts, credit activity, checkout records, cookies, support messages, and private album access.

2. No AI training on your photos

Your uploaded photos, prompts, and generated private results are used to provide the AIVideosUGC service you request. They are never used to train models or build public datasets.

3. 30-day auto-delete for input photos

Input photos automatically delete 30 days after generation. Generated results, billing records, security logs, dispute records, and support messages may be retained where needed for account access, legal compliance, fraud prevention, refunds, and customer support.

4. AES-256 encryption at rest · TLS encryption in transit

AIVideosUGC protects private uploads and account data with AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS encryption in transit across the stack. Access checks, scoped sessions, security cookies, monitoring, and provider controls reduce unauthorized access.

5. Payments, credits, and service providers

Payments may be processed by Stripe or another connected provider. Hosting, storage, email, moderation, analytics, payment, and AI infrastructure providers may process limited data only to run, secure, generate, store, or deliver the requested service.

6. Compliance references

Separate Children's Privacy and State Privacy notices explain child-related requests and regional privacy rights that may apply to your use of the service.

7. Your choices and contact

You may ask for access, correction, export, deletion, or help with account privacy. Email support@aivideosugc.com with your account email and request details. We may verify account ownership before acting on sensitive requests.

@graph.name: AI Promo Video Maker | AIVideosUGC
@graph.description: Generate promo videos from a product link or one photo. Add a script, an AI avatar, and a voice, then export a tall, square, or wide file to post.

@graph.name: How to Make a Promo Video in 3 Simple Steps

step.name: Upload Your Product Photo
step.text: Upload one photo of the finished product, or paste the product page. The announcement keeps that item in frame.

step.name: Describe Your Scene
step.text: Describe the scene, or keep the details from the link, and name the offer. You get a line you can fix before it renders.

step.name: Download and Post
step.text: Download your promo in the right size and post it; compare openings in your performance dashboard and keep the version that performs best.

mainEntity.name: Can I use my brand assets in a promo video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Upload your product photos and brand assets to give the promo a consistent look. Use only images and marks you have rights to use.

mainEntity.name: Can a beginner make a promo video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Upload a clear phone photo or paste a product link, then choose a style and message. You can make a promo without editing experience.

mainEntity.name: What is included in a product launch video template?

acceptedAnswer.text: It gives you a product reveal you can customize with a voice, captions, and different openings. Export a vertical, square, or wide version for your channel.

mainEntity.name: Who should use a launch template?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is useful for shops launching a new product and needing ads quickly. Start with a product photo or link instead of booking a studio.

mainEntity.name: Why use a template instead of filming a creator?

acceptedAnswer.text: A template lets you update the message and make another launch video in minutes. You can test several openings without paying for another shoot.

mainEntity.name: Can an AI actor present my promo video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Choose an AI actor to present your product with a voice. You can make a launch video without hiring a presenter or filming yourself.

mainEntity.name: How do credits work for a promo video?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 6, 10, 15, or 30 second video costs 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits. Starter costs $24.50 monthly for 200 credits, Pro $35 for 300, and Premium $63 for 600. Failed jobs return their credits.

mainEntity.name: How does a promo video maker work for different products?

acceptedAnswer.text: Paste a product link or upload a photo, and the promo video uses those details to feature your item. Review the message before posting.

mainEntity.name: Can I automate promo videos from product links?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Paste a product page link to start a promo video with its images and details. You can make versions for many products through the API.

mainEntity.name: Can the launch clip run in ads and for clients?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Finished launch videos have no watermark and can be used in paid ads or client work. Make sure you have rights to the assets you upload.

mainEntity.name: Which channels can the launch clip fit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose 9:16 for Stories and Reels, 1:1 for feeds, or 16:9 for wide placements. Review each version on the screen where it will appear.

settings.title: Cookie policy

settings.body: This policy explains the cookies and local storage used on www.aidreamcapes.com for the Aidreamcapes AI photo and video service.
settings.title: How cookies support sign-in, checkout, and private albums.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. Aidreamcapes also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo and video service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps Aidreamcapes open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, Aidreamcapes may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@aidreamcapes.com with cookie or tracking questions.

settings.body:
1. What cookies are

Cookies are small files stored by your browser. AIVideosUGC also uses similar browser storage, such as local storage, to keep the AI photo and video service secure, usable, and consistent while you move between packages, checkout, your account, and private albums.

2. Essential cookies

Essential cookies support customer sign-in, scoped sessions, CSRF protection, checkout continuity, credit reservation flows, private album access, rate limiting, fraud prevention, and secure admin or customer authentication. These cookies are required for the core service and cannot be switched off inside the site without breaking key features.

3. Preference storage

We may remember practical preferences such as menu state, recently opened workspace views, selected package context, language or display choices if available, and browser-side UI settings. This helps AIVideosUGC open the right customer workspace more quickly.

4. Performance and diagnostics

We may collect limited technical signals to understand slow pages, failed requests, broken checkout steps, job submission errors, and account access issues. These signals help us improve route speed, generation reliability, and customer support.

5. Analytics and measurement

If analytics tools are enabled, they may help us understand aggregated usage such as popular package categories, tool discovery, pricing page visits, and conversion paths. Analytics should not be used to sell your uploaded photos or generated images.

6. Payment, email, hosting, and AI providers

Connected providers may set or read cookies or similar identifiers when needed for checkout, anti-fraud checks, email delivery, hosting security, media storage, or AI generation. Their use is limited to providing and protecting the requested service.

7. Your browser controls

You can block, delete, or limit cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, AIVideosUGC may not be able to keep you signed in, complete checkout, reserve credits, start generation jobs, or open private albums.

8. Relationship to privacy policy

Cookie data is handled together with the privacy practices described in our Privacy Policy. The Terms of Service explain customer responsibilities when using accounts, credits, uploads, and generated outputs.

9. Updates and contact

We may update this Cookie Policy as we add or remove providers, analytics, checkout methods, or security features. Email support@aivideosugc.com with cookie or tracking questions.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Make separate ads for many products in your catalog. Change the message or actor to test more versions without filming each item.

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose a tool that makes scripts, actors, voices, and ad sizes from your product. AIVideosUGC also lets you make many versions for testing.

mainEntity.name: How do these compare with ads filmed by creators?

acceptedAnswer.text: Results vary by product and audience. AI ads are useful for quick tests and many versions; a filmed creator suits campaigns needing a real person.

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload a product photo or paste a link, then review the script and choose an actor. Download the finished ad in minutes.

mainEntity.name: Which frame sizes and placements can the file use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Download square videos (1:1), portrait videos (9:16), or landscape videos (16:9) for TikTok, Meta, YouTube, and your store.

mainEntity.name: What does a video ads generator produce?

acceptedAnswer.text: It makes a finished video ad from a product photo, link, or short description. Add an AI actor, voice, and script without filming.

mainEntity.name: Are commercial rights included on a paid plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your watermark-free video is cleared for commercial use, including paid ads. You do not need a separate license for an AIVideosUGC AI actor.

mainEntity.name: How much does an AI video ad cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Video credits depend on length: 6 seconds costs 24, 10 costs 40, 15 costs 60, and 30 costs 120. Starter costs $24.50 for 200 credits.

acceptedAnswer.text: AI video ads can run on Meta and TikTok, subject to their current rules. Check whether your ad needs an AI label before posting.

1. Agreement to these terms

These Terms of Service apply when you visit www.aidreamcapes.com, create a Aidreamcapes account, upload photos, buy credits or subscriptions, use AI photo and video tools, start generation jobs, download outputs, or access private albums.

2. Accounts, credits, and checkout

You are responsible for accurate account information and secure sign-in. Credits are added after payment confirmation, displayed before generation, reserved when a request begins, used after successful delivery, and released or reviewed when a request fails.

3. Upload rights and consent

You may upload only photos, reference images, prompts, or other materials that you own or have permission to use. Do not upload photos of minors or non-consenting people unless you have the legal right and consent required for the requested use. Do not upload photos of public figures, protected marks, stolen images, or other materials without the rights or permissions required for the requested use, or that violate law, platform rules, or third-party rights.

4. No AI training on your photos

Your inputs are never used to train models. 30-day auto-delete applies to input photos after generation. Private uploads and account records are protected with AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS encryption in transit. Some billing, security, tax, dispute, refund, and account-integrity records may be retained where required or reasonably necessary.

5. AI output variability

AI photo and video results can vary based on source photo quality, pose, lighting, package settings, moderation review, provider availability, and model behavior. Aidreamcapes may reject, rerun, delay, moderate, or remove jobs that violate rules or cannot be completed reliably.

6. Private albums and use of outputs

Generated images and albums are designed for private customer access unless you choose to share, publish, or download them. You are responsible for reviewing outputs before using them in advertising, profiles, documents, merchandise, social media, or other public settings.

7. Refunds and guarantee review

Refunds and credit adjustments follow the Refund Policy, including a results-based refund review when a result does not look like you, subject to the conditions and review process described in that policy.

8. Contact

Email support@aidreamcapes.com for account, billing, refund, policy, or legal questions.

Customers may upload only photos, reference images, prompts, logos, or creative direction they own or have permission to use. Private photo packages should be based on lawful, consented source material.

2. Identity consent

Do not upload or request content involving minors, non-consenting people, stolen images, public figures, celebrities, athletes, official marks, trademarks, or protected brand assets without permission. Do not use AIVideosUGC for impersonation, harassment, deception, exploitation, fake evidence, or unlawful activity.

3. No AI training on your photos

Your inputs are never used to train models.

4. 30-day auto-delete for input photos

Input photos automatically delete 30 days after generation.

5. AES-256 encryption at rest · TLS encryption in transit

Private uploads and generated account records are handled with AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS encryption in transit across the stack.

6. Moderation and blocked requests

AIVideosUGC may review, reject, remove, rerun, or limit requests that appear unsafe, unauthorized, misleading, infringing, exploitative, or outside supported personal, creator, or business workflows.

7. Responsible output use

AI outputs can contain artifacts or inaccurate details. Review results before posting, selling, printing, or using them for profiles, campaigns, documents, or social platforms. You remain responsible for following rights, disclosure, and platform rules.

8. Reporting concerns

Email support@aivideosugc.com with the account email, page, package, job, or gallery details if content should be reviewed or removed.

step.text: Upload the garment flat, with the collar, cuffs, and hem in frame. That outline is what the move has to keep.

mainEntity.name: Which frame and length can I download?

acceptedAnswer.text: Download 6, 10, 15, or 30 second videos in sizes including 9:16, 1:1, and 16:9. Pick the size your ad placement needs.

mainEntity.name: Can I use them if I have never edited a video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Upload your apparel photos, choose a message, and make the ad. You do not need filming or editing experience.

mainEntity.name: How does a clothing template build the ad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upload your clothing photos and choose a message. The template builds a video with an opening, voice, and scenes for apparel shoppers.

mainEntity.name: What are clothing video ad templates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clothing video ad templates are prebuilt formats that show apparel worn and styled. Add your product photos to make an ad in minutes without a model shoot.

mainEntity.name: Can I run the reel as an ad or in another language?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Post your watermark-free reel as an ad and make another version in a different language. Use the same clothing photos.

mainEntity.name: Can I make several versions for different styles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Make versions for different outfits, seasons, and buyers from the same photos. You can test new openings without another shoot.

mainEntity.name: Who should use these clothing templates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clothing shops and fashion marketers can use these templates for regular ads. Make fresh videos without booking models or studios.

mainEntity.name: What clothing can these templates cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: These templates cover streetwear, casualwear, activewear, and occasion wear. Use the format that best shows how your item looks on a person.

mainEntity.name: How fast can I get a clothing video ad?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can make a clothing video ad in a few minutes from product photos. There is no model booking or studio wait.

mainEntity.name: How many credits does a clothing video cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 6-second video uses 24 credits; 10, 15, and 30 seconds use 40, 60, and 120. Failed jobs return credits.

seo.title: AI Talking Photo Video Guide for Creators | Aidreamcapes
seo.keywords: AI talking photo, talking portrait video, AI avatar video, talking photo safety
seo.description: Use this AI talking photo guide to plan portraits, scripts, consent, disclosure, review steps, and publishing choices before sharing a generated video.

settings.body:
A talking photo video uses a person’s likeness, so permission, context, and review belong in the workflow from the first upload. Choose an authorized portrait, write the exact script, check the voice and lip movement, and tell the audience enough about the generated media when misunderstanding is possible. The safest process separates what the source person approved from what the generated performance adds. That preparation makes the final clip easier to review and explain.

Start with a permission-safe portrait

Use a face you own or have permission to animate. Keep the permission record with the project and define the intended audience, channel, duration, and message. A portrait can be technically suitable and still be unsuitable for the planned use if the permission does not cover the message or placement.

Choose a recent, front-facing image with readable eyes, mouth, hairline, and lighting. Avoid a crop where the mouth is hidden or a strong shadow changes the face. If the photo includes other people, private details, or a recognizable location, treat those elements as part of the rights review too.

Write the exact words before generating

Keep the script short enough to review line by line. Mark names, numbers, pronunciation, pauses, and the intended language. Short sentences make it easier to compare the audio, captions, lip timing, and meaning without losing track of a late edit.

Do not write a script that makes the generated person appear to confess, endorse, report, or speak on a topic they did not approve. If a brand or organization is speaking, define who owns the message and how the viewer should understand the presenter.

Treat audio and captions as first-class content

Review pronunciation, names, numbers, pauses, volume, background noise, and timing. Compare captions with the approved script rather than trusting automatic transcription. A clear face does not make an incorrect sentence acceptable.

For a different language or audience, use the Multilingual Video workflow as a planning reference, then have a fluent reviewer check names, idioms, captions, and timing. Translation is a content change, not only an audio change.

Review identity and movement frame by frame

Watch for mouth shapes that do not match the audio, eye direction that changes unexpectedly, unstable hair or jewelry, skin-tone shifts, and face edges that break during movement. Pause at the beginning, end, and any sentence with a strong expression or turn.

If the project needs a presenter-led message rather than an animated portrait, compare the result with the Founder Update workflow. Choose the format based on the communication job, not only on how easy the first generation looks.

Decide what context the viewer needs

Disclosure should be clear enough for the audience and placement to understand when the media is generated or substantially altered. The exact wording depends on the channel and the situation, so keep the context honest and review it with the destination copy.

Do not use a generated talking photo to make a real person appear to say something they did not authorize. Keep the approved portrait, permission, script, final export, and disclosure decision together so later edits remain traceable.

A practical publishing checklist

  • The portrait, voice, script, and intended use are authorized.
  • Names, numbers, pronunciation, language, captions, and pauses match the approved script.
  • Face, mouth, eyes, hair, skin tone, and framing remain stable through the clip.
  • Disclosure and audience context do not imply an unapproved real-person statement.
  • The final export and permission record are stored together with the review decision.

Choose the right workflow

NeedWorkflowPrimary review
Animate an approved portraitTalking PhotoLikeness, permission, lip movement, and disclosure
Present a direct-to-camera speakerTalking Head VideoIdentity, performance, framing, and message ownership
Adapt the approved message for another languageMultilingual VideoNames, pronunciation, translation, captions, and timing

FAQ

Can I animate any portrait I find online?

No. Use a portrait you own or have permission to animate for the intended use. Public availability is not the same as permission to create a speaking or endorsing likeness.

What makes a talking photo video ready to share?

The source permission, script, audio, captions, face movement, disclosure, audience, and destination should all be reviewed. A technically smooth clip is not ready if its context or message is misleading.

How can I reduce lip-sync problems?

Use a clear front-facing portrait, a focused script, and short sentences. Review the final audio and mouth movement together, especially around names, numbers, pauses, and translated words.

When should I use a talking head workflow instead?

Use a talking head format when the communication needs a fuller presenter, direct-to-camera framing, or a different performance style. The choice should follow the message and permission available for the source.

Do I always need an AI disclosure?

Review the expectations of the channel, audience, and applicable policy. Add clear context when viewers could reasonably mistake generated or substantially altered media for an unedited real statement or recording.

Aidreamcapes can help create the visual format, but permission and editorial responsibility stay with the publisher. Keep the workflow reviewable from source portrait to final share so the audience can understand what the video represents.

sections.h2: How Do I Review a Finished Video Ad?
paras: Watch the file the way a shopper will, on a phone, with the sound and the captions on. Start from the first frame.
A TikTok ad and a Meta ad both need the product to match. Meta here means Facebook and Instagram. A tall file and a square file can still show the same product.

paras: Hold the real product, or your original photo, next to the screen and go through color, shape, logos, parts, and size.

Compare the color in daylight. Count the parts. Read every letter on a label. If a hand is in the picture, the product should look the right size next to it. Extra scenery is fine only when a shopper can tell it is not part of the order. Those scenes are made as [lifestyle product photos](/ai-image-generation/lifestyle-scene).

paras: Play the clip on your phone. Listen to the voice, and read the captions. Then watch the hands and the first frame.

The script should name the product you ship. Do not mention a feature that is not for sale. Clips often go wrong while the product moves. Count the fingers, and watch how they hold the item. If one short moment looks wrong, trim it. If the problem runs through the whole clip, make a new version. Run this check on a [product video](/ai-video-generation/product-video) before you post it.

paras: Upload only photos you took, or photos you have permission to use. Use only logos that belong to you.

seo.title: Ecommerce Product Image Workflow
seo.keywords: ecommerce product image workflow, product page images, AI product content, PDP image checklist
seo.description: Build an ecommerce product image workflow from an approved source to main image, lifestyle scene, feature graphic, and comparison asset with review gates.

settings.body:
An ecommerce product page usually needs a set of images, not one oversized hero. Plan the questions the gallery must answer, assign each question to one asset, and use the same approved product reference across the set. This workflow keeps the main image clear, gives supporting images a distinct job, and creates review gates before the gallery reaches a PDP, marketplace listing, ad, or social campaign. It also keeps the gallery coherent from first click to checkout.

Map shopper questions to image roles

Start with the decisions a shopper must make: what the item is, how it is used, what it includes, how large it is, which feature matters, and how variants compare. Do not create five versions of the same decorative scene when the page is missing a basic answer such as scale or included items.

Write the role beside each planned asset. The role becomes the review criterion: a main image must identify the product, a feature graphic must explain only approved information, and a comparison chart must make the difference between options clear without changing their specifications.

Keep one approved source of truth

Use one product reference and one fact sheet across the image set. Record colors, dimensions, materials, included items, variant names, and text that must remain exact. If the source changes, mark which outputs need review rather than quietly mixing old and new versions.

A stable source does not mean every image must be identical. It means the object, package, and facts stay recognizable while the composition changes to answer a different question. Store the source ID or filename in the approval record for traceability.

Create the set in a useful sequence

Create the clearest product-first image before adding context. Then fill information gaps with a lifestyle view, feature explanation, size cue, or comparison asset. Sequencing the work this way makes it easier to notice when a decorative image is compensating for a missing product fact.

The Ecommerce Main Image is a useful starting point. Add a Feature Infographic when a visual explanation helps, and use a Comparison Chart only when the variants and comparison facts are available.

Review the gallery at the size shoppers see

Check the first frame, thumbnail sequence, mobile crop, and text legibility. A feature label that works on a large desktop canvas may be unreadable in a gallery. Make sure the image order tells a coherent story without forcing the viewer to infer what is included.

Look for product drift between images: a handle changes shape, a color becomes warmer, a package gains an item, or a lifestyle prop makes the item appear larger than it is. Remove an asset when the visual suggestion is stronger than the verified product fact.

Separate channel variants from product truth

A PDP, marketplace feed, paid social ad, and email may require different dimensions or crops. Create those variants from the approved set, and keep the product representation stable. Do not let a platform-specific crop remove the disclaimer, size cue, or product detail needed to understand the image.

Record the destination for every exported asset. This makes it possible to update a campaign variant without accidentally replacing the main product image or carrying a promotional claim into an evergreen page.

A practical publishing checklist

  • Every planned image has one shopper question and one review criterion.
  • The same approved source and fact sheet are used across the set.
  • Main image, context, feature, size, and comparison assets are not redundant.
  • Text, dimensions, colors, included items, and variant differences remain accurate.
  • The complete set has been reviewed in the actual PDP, mobile crop, and campaign placement.

Choose the right workflow

Gallery roleRecommended workflowDo not use it to
Identify the productEcommerce Main ImageAdd unsupported lifestyle or performance claims
Explain a verified featureFeature InfographicInvent specifications or unreadable labels
Clarify variant differencesComparison ChartReplace a missing fact sheet or current option data

FAQ

How many product images should an ecommerce page have?

There is no universal number. Start with the shopper questions the page must answer and add only the assets that provide distinct information. A smaller accurate set is better than a larger set with repeated or misleading scenes.

Which image should I create first?

Create the clearest product-first image first. It establishes the reference for later lifestyle, feature, size, and comparison assets and exposes source problems before more work is built on top of them.

When should I use a feature infographic?

Use one when a verified feature is easier to understand visually than in a paragraph. Keep the text and visual labels tied to the product facts and review them at mobile size.

How do I avoid inconsistent AI product images?

Keep one approved source and fact sheet, reuse the product reference, define the role of each asset, and compare outputs as a set. Reject any image that changes shape, color, scale, packaging, or included items.

Can the same image be used on a product page and in an ad?

Sometimes, but review the crop, claims, destination, and channel requirements separately. A page image may need detail while an ad needs a faster visual hook; the product truth should remain the same.

Use the workflow to organize the gallery around shopper decisions, not around the number of generations available. The final collection should make the product clearer from the first thumbnail through the last supporting asset.

seo.title: AI Content Disclosure and Safe Usage
seo.keywords: AI content disclosure, safe AI usage, synthetic media policy, permission-safe AI content
seo.description: Review AI content responsibly with permission-safe sources, honest context, disclosure decisions, rights checks, and a record of final approval.

settings.body:
Responsible AI content starts before generation and continues after export. Use permission-safe source material, keep product and personal claims tied to approved facts, describe generated or substantially altered media honestly when context matters, and retain a review record. The goal is not a single label that solves every situation; it is a repeatable decision process that keeps the source, message, audience, and publishing context connected. The same record helps teams explain why a final asset was approved.

Start with permission-safe source material

Use photos, voices, products, logos, text, and locations that you own or are authorized to use for the intended purpose. Keep the permission scope visible to the team. A source that is acceptable for an internal concept may not be approved for an advertisement, public profile, or impersonation-sensitive message.

The Professional Headshot workflow can help organize a portrait task, but the workflow does not grant rights to a person’s likeness. Store the source and authorization together before generation.

Separate the visual treatment from message ownership

AI can change a scene, animate a portrait, or create a campaign variation. It does not decide who is allowed to speak, endorse, promise, or disclose. Define the message owner and compare every visible or spoken claim with the approved source.

Be careful with names, voices, faces, testimonials, product results, and institutional statements. A realistic presentation can increase the chance that a viewer mistakes a generated scene for a real record or an authorized statement.

Add the context the audience needs

Disclosure should be clear enough for the audience and placement to understand when content is generated or substantially altered and that difference could affect interpretation. Review the caption, thumbnail, surrounding copy, and destination rather than placing all responsibility on a small label.

The right context depends on the channel and message. Avoid making a universal legal promise in the article; instead, direct the team to review the current Content Policy and the requirements of the destination where the material will appear.

Review rights, accuracy, and audience expectations

Check factual claims, names, faces, voices, brand marks, private details, product appearance, and destination links. Consider what a reasonable viewer could infer from the complete presentation. If the generated result suggests a different product, relationship, location, or event, revise it even if no single sentence is technically false.

For brand storytelling, the Founder Update workflow can organize the narrative, but the final review still belongs to the publisher. Generated polish should not replace a source check or rights review.

Keep a record that can survive the next edit

Keep the approved source, brief or script, final export, disclosure decision, audience, destination, reviewer, and date together. When a channel or product fact changes, the record tells the team which assets need another review.

Remove content that is misleading, unsafe, outside the approved use, or impossible to explain clearly. A smaller approved library is easier to maintain than a large folder of files with unknown sources and uncertain context.

A practical publishing checklist

  • The source material, likenesses, voices, logos, and text are authorized for the intended use.
  • The message owner has approved the factual claims and implied meaning.
  • Disclosure and surrounding context match the audience, channel, and destination.
  • The final asset has been checked for rights, accuracy, privacy, and misleading visual suggestions.
  • The source, final export, reviewer, date, and decision are recorded together.

Choose the right workflow

QuestionUse this referenceStill required
What may be uploaded or published?Content PolicyCheck current permission and destination requirements
How should a portrait be prepared?Professional HeadshotObtain and retain likeness authorization
How should a brand story be structured?Brand VideoVerify claims, rights, disclosure, and audience context

FAQ

What does permission-safe AI content mean?

It means the source material and intended use are authorized, and the generated result does not extend that authorization into an unapproved statement, endorsement, or private disclosure.

When should AI-generated content be disclosed?

Review whether the generated or altered nature could affect how the audience interprets the content, and follow the current policy and destination requirements. Include clear context when a viewer could reasonably mistake the result for an unedited real record or statement.

Is a generated person automatically a real endorsement?

No. A generated performance should not be presented as a real customer, employee, spokesperson, or public figure unless the relationship and authorization are accurate. Avoid invented testimonials and implied approval.

Should the disclosure appear in the image or video itself?

The placement depends on the channel and audience, but review the complete experience: asset, caption, surrounding copy, thumbnail, and destination. Do not hide material context where it could change interpretation.

What should I keep after publishing?

Keep the approved source, brief or script, final export, rights notes, disclosure decision, reviewer, date, audience, and destination. This makes future edits and product changes easier to recheck.

Use Aidreamcapes workflows to create and organize content, then apply a human review that matches the stakes of the audience and message. Responsible publishing is a chain of decisions, not a single generated output.

seo.title: AI Motion Generator Video Guide
seo.keywords: AI motion generator, image to video workflow, product motion video, AI video review
seo.description: Plan motion-generator videos from one approved image with a focused action, continuity checks, product-safe movement, and final export review.

settings.body:
A motion-generator video starts with a still image, but a useful result needs more than movement. Choose one visible action, define what must stay fixed, and review the transition from the first frame to the last. The best brief gives the generator room to animate the scene while protecting the product’s identity, proportions, text, and intended context. Treat the output as a new video asset that still needs rights, claims, and export review.

Choose a still that can support motion

Use an approved image with a clear subject, stable edges, and enough separation between the product and background. A busy crop, hidden handle, reflective surface, or tiny label gives the motion workflow more ambiguity to resolve. If the product must remain exact, start with the clearest source rather than the most decorative one.

Record the source file and the details that must not change: shape, color, logo, packaging, included parts, and relative scale. A motion clip can be visually engaging while still failing if the source product becomes a different object halfway through.

Describe one readable action

Choose one movement such as a slow camera push, a controlled turn, a gentle fabric shift, or a small environmental change. Explain the direction, speed, start frame, end frame, and what remains still. A single action is easier to judge than a brief that asks the product, camera, background, and lighting to transform at once.

Avoid movement that implies a product capability the source does not establish. A generated opening, pour, stretch, or interaction should not become evidence of how the item works unless the real product facts and review support that interpretation.

Protect continuity across the clip

Review the product silhouette, edges, texture, reflections, labels, hands, and background at the beginning, middle, and end. Look for added parts, disappearing text, warped geometry, changing colors, and camera motion that makes the product appear to change size.

For a more controlled product-first treatment, compare the brief with the Product Video workflow. For a mood-led scene, the Cinematic Video workflow may be a better fit, but the same product continuity checks still apply.

Review motion at normal speed and frame by frame

Watch once for the viewer’s overall impression, then pause on the moments where the subject turns, intersects with a hand, or crosses a high-contrast edge. Check whether the motion communicates the intended idea and whether a viewer could infer a false feature, scale, or use.

Check audio, captions, thumbnail, aspect ratio, and destination when they are part of the final package. Motion quality is only one part of publishing quality; an otherwise clean clip can still carry an outdated CTA or unsupported claim.

Keep source, motion brief, and export connected

Save the approved still, motion description, selected output, reviewer, and destination together. If the team requests a shorter or vertical version, create it from the approved source and record a new review rather than overwriting the original decision.

Use the Motion Generator as the direct starting point for a single-image movement concept. Move to a different video workflow when the job is a product demonstration, talking portrait, or multi-scene narrative so the brief and review criteria match the asset.

A practical publishing checklist

  • The source still, product facts, and intended use are approved.
  • One readable action and one stable subject are defined in the motion brief.
  • Product silhouette, color, label, packaging, scale, and included parts remain consistent.
  • The exported file has been checked for claims, audio, captions, crop, thumbnail, and CTA.
  • The source, brief, output, reviewer, destination, and version are recorded together.

Choose the right workflow

Creative jobWorkflowBest fit
Animate one approved stillMotion GeneratorA focused movement with a stable subject
Show a product in a controlled sequenceProduct VideoProduct clarity and demonstration context
Build a mood-led visual treatmentCinematic VideoAtmosphere, camera language, and scene direction

FAQ

What image works best for a motion-generator video?

Use an approved, clear image with a stable subject, visible edges, and enough separation from the background. Include the product details that must remain unchanged during movement.

How much movement should I request?

Start with one readable action and define what remains still. A focused camera move or environmental change is easier to review than several simultaneous transformations.

How do I prevent product shape drift?

Use a clear source, state the fixed details in the brief, avoid overloading the action, and review the silhouette, labels, reflections, and scale at several points in the clip.

When should I use Product Video instead?

Use Product Video when the asset needs a controlled product demonstration, a sequence of product views, or stronger product-first framing than a single motion concept provides.

Can I publish the first good-looking output?

Review the exported file first. Check continuity, claims, rights, captions, audio, crop, thumbnail, destination, and audience context before sharing or placing it in a campaign.

Motion Generator is most reliable as a focused transformation of an approved still. Keep the action legible, protect the product truth, and treat every export as a reviewable publishing asset.

mainEntity.name: Can I choose the actor, voice, and language?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Choose from 53 AI actors, pick a voice, and write in the language your customers use. You may use your own voice sample if you have permission.

mainEntity.name: Where can I use an AI actor video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use it on product pages, in paid ads, on social media, or in training. You can download it without a watermark and make versions for different channels.

mainEntity.name: How can a digital actor present my product?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI actors are lifelike digital presenters who speak about your product on video. You choose the face, voice, and language without arranging a photo shoot.

mainEntity.name: How can shops use digital presenters on social media?

acceptedAnswer.text: Make short product videos with the same actor so your posts look consistent. Try different openings or offers for each audience without hiring a creator.

mainEntity.name: Can an AI actor explain my product?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. An AI actor can explain a product feature clearly and give the same message in every video. You can change the words without another shoot.

mainEntity.name: How do AI actors make videos?

acceptedAnswer.text: Write what you want said, choose an actor and voice, and generate the video. The actor speaks your words with matching mouth movements in a few minutes.

mainEntity.name: What should I check before posting an AI actor video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check that your product claims are accurate and follow the ad platform’s rules for AI content. Use only photos and voice samples you have permission to upload.

mainEntity.name: Can I update an AI actor training video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Change the words when your instructions change and make a new video. You can also make versions in other languages without filming again.

mainEntity.name: Can I use AI actor videos in paid ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. AI actor videos can run in paid ads and have no watermark. You need rights to the product photos and voice samples you upload.

mainEntity.name: Does a video include a spoken line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your video can include a spoken message, editable captions, and music. Choose an AI actor to present it without recording yourself.

mainEntity.name: Can I start from a product page link?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Paste a public product page link to bring in its photos and details. Review the message and scene before making the ad.

mainEntity.name: How many AI actors are in the library?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are 53 AI actors in the library. Choose one that fits your audience and use them again across several ads.

mainEntity.name: What length and shape can the ad use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds and a format such as vertical, square, or wide. You can make versions for different feeds from the same product photo.

mainEntity.name: What can I make with AIVideosUGC?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can make store images and short product ads from a photo or link. Add an AI actor, voice, and captions when the message needs a presenter.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a crew, or just a product photo?

acceptedAnswer.text: No crew is needed. Start with a product photo or public link, choose the message and actor, and make an ad in minutes.

mainEntity.name: What does AIVideosUGC cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Starter costs $24.50 monthly for 200 credits; Pro costs $35 for 300; Premium costs $63 for 600. You see each job’s credit cost before starting, and failed jobs return their credits.

mainEntity.name: Do I pay before the first file?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Choose Starter at $24.50 monthly for 200 credits, Pro at $35 for 300, or Premium at $63 for 600. You see the credit cost before each job.

mainEntity.name: Can I make more than one version at a time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Make several versions from one product photo to test different messages or actors. You see the credit cost for each version before starting.

mainEntity.name: Can I send the file to TikTok or Meta from the tool?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can send a finished file to TikTok, Instagram, or Facebook from the tool, or download it and post it yourself.

mainEntity.name: How many credits does a video or photo use?

acceptedAnswer.text: A photo costs 24 credits. A 6, 10, 15, or 30 second video costs 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits. Failed jobs return their credits.

mainEntity.name: Can my own software start a photo or video?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your software can start photo or video jobs through the API. Email support@aivideosugc.com to get access.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to choose a video model?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Choose the result you want, add your product photo or link, and make the video. You can review and adjust it before posting.

mainEntity.name: Can I reuse the same actor on the next ad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Choose from 53 AI actors and use the same presenter in another ad. This keeps your product videos consistent without arranging another shoot.

mainEntity.name: Can I rebuild an ad I already run?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Use an ad you already run as a reference, then change the opening or actor for your product. This helps you test another version quickly.

mainEntity.name: Can the actor say the line in another language?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Write the message in the language your customers use and choose a matching voice. You can make a new version without hiring another presenter.

mainEntity.name: What is AIVideosUGC?

acceptedAnswer.text: AIVideosUGC turns your product photos or links into store images and short video ads. Add an AI actor and voice when you want someone to present the product.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the results in ads and on my store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Download the file without a watermark for your store or paid ads. Follow each platform’s rules when you post.
